scenes.text: A hanging box pulls this box on the table through string over a pulley. A particle keeps mass but ignores size. We track translation. If it tips, size matters. Air resistance neglected means no drag. Include air resistance, and drag changes the resultant.

scenes.text: Light means negligible mass. A light string needs no force to accelerate itself. A heavy string does. A light pulley has negligible rotational inertia. A massive pulley resists spin changes. A smooth pulley has no friction. Together, these give equal tensions. A rough pulley can make them unequal.

scenes.text: Inextensible means fixed length. While taut, any length gained here is lost there, so the boxes have equal speed and acceleration magnitudes, in different directions. An extensible string stretches, breaking that link. A slack string cannot pull or push, so it gives neither tension nor linked motion.

scenes.text: These other words describe parts of our example. Paper Four treats bodies as particles. turning effects here are extra context. A rigid rod, like this brace, keeps its shape, so it can push or pull. A flexible brace bends. A light rod ignores its own mass. A heavy one adds weight. A beam keeps force positions because they affect turning. Uniform means evenly spread mass. A uniform rod balances at its midpoint. Uneven mass shifts that point. A lamina is a thin sheet, like this label. Ignore thickness. A thick plate needs depth. A uniform lamina balances at its area centroid. Uneven mass shifts it. A bead follows a wire's path. Detached, it can leave. The wire ignores thickness. A thick guide needs clearance. Smooth contact gives a perpendicular reaction. Rough contact adds friction. A fixed peg can replace the pulley. Moving it changes the path constraint. A smooth peg preserves tension with light string. A rough peg may not.

beats.text: Let's find the acceleration and tension. The table box is three kilograms.
Two kilograms hangs; its weight drives the motion.
Use g equals ten metres per second squared: gravitational acceleration.
The forces: box weight down, reaction up, tension right. Hanging weight down, tension up. Vertical forces on the table box balance.
Why these equations?
Resultant force equals mass times acceleration. For the smooth table box, tension alone gives three a.
For the hanging box, weight minus tension gives two a: downward is positive.
Add: equal tensions cancel. Five kilograms is the total moving mass.
What acceleration follows?
Four metres per second squared. Each box gains four metres per second every second.
And tension?
Substitute into T equals three a. Twelve newtons: the pull on either box.

scenes.text: A plane models our table as flat and rigid. On a curved or bending surface, the contact direction changes. Smooth means no friction, so contact gives only the perpendicular reaction. What changes if our table is rough? Rough allows friction. Our box slides right, so friction opposes that slide. Tension minus friction now accelerates the box. Add the unchanged hanging equation. two g minus F equals five a. Less driving force means less acceleration. Question. Does rough always mean F equals mu R? No. Below the limit, static friction adjusts. Equality needs limiting friction, or the stated sliding model. Choose, solve, interpret, check size, sign, units and plausibility. Refine.
